newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania committees want clarity on elections.
newsitem.headline: Albania committees want clarity on elections.

text.p: Albania's salvation committees, maverick bands that formed amid riots in February and March, again postponed a decision to disband on Saturday, saying they wanted clarity over planned elections.

A national committee which says it represents 20 groups throughout the Balkan state said it wanted to know whether political parties would carry out a threat to boycott elections planned for the end of June.

The committees came together amid the rioting and violence to try to bring some order to parts of the chaotic country where the state's authority had collapsed. Reports of their influence, with some southern residents saying it has declined since the riots ended.

The committees, which were to disband this week under a deal brokered by European envoy Franz Vranitzky, were meeting in this port town in southern Albania, one of the epicentres of the March disturbances.
The elections were called to restore order to Albania, after anger over the collapse of crooked pyramid investment schemes erupted into riots and anarchy in February and March.
They were also still directing their anger against President Sali Berisha, whom many people blame for the collapse of the schemes and the loss of their money.

"We are still here to meet opposition parties to reach a common view on whether to participate in elections...But if people want us to fight right now against Berisha, we are ready for it," said Xhevat Kocia, head of the national committee.
Most parties of a national unity government threatened to boycott the vote in a dispute on election laws, which they say favours Berisha and his former ruling Democratic Party.
The parties were holding crisis talks in Tirana to find a compromise that would allow elections to go ahead.
A committee leader said there were no plans to unseat Berisha by force as he was so unpopular they were not needed.
"Everwhere you go you meet people looking forward to seeing Berisha out," Albert Shyti, leader of the Vlore committee.
